indian.headline: Indian markets closed slightly down on mixed sentiment; FPI inflows and rupee strength offset weak banking stocks.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed slightly down on mixed sentiment; FPI inflows and rupee strength offset weak banking stocks.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.22%, Nifty 50 dropped 0.14%, and Bank Nifty slid 0.41% as banking and pharma sectors weakened, though IT stocks gained 0.2%.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities ended a subdued session in the red, with the Sensex, Nifty 50, and Bank Nifty all posting modest losses. The banking sector dragged the most, sinking 0.4%, while IT stocks bucked the trend with a 0.2% gain and pharma slipped 0.1%. The rupee opened stronger at 95.64 per dollar, buoyed by robust capital inflows and RBI support measures. Foreign investors returned aggressively, having purchased ₹43,744 crore in July-August after months of heavy selling, signalling renewed confidence in Indian equities despite the day's weakness.

The market remained range-bound with mixed IPO activity: Horizon Industrial Parks listed flat while Hy-Tech Engineers opened with strong grey market premiums hinting a 47% listing gain. Against this backdrop, SEBI data painted a cautionary picture—over 90% of retail derivatives traders lose money, with 89% of traders under 30 losing cash in FY26. Separately, SoftBank Vision Fund offloaded a 2.6% stake in Lenskart for $300 million, and US sanctions threats on Iran kept oil prices elevated, pressuring government bond yields.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: US Iran sanctions threaten higher oil and bond yields; FPI inflows continue despite selling elsewhere.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: FPIs purchased ₹43,744 crore in July-August; SoftBank trimmed Lenskart stake via block deal.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: US Iran sanctions keep prices elevated, pressuring Indian bond yields and inflation outlook.

indian.watch: Bank Nifty recovery, IPO listing performance (Hy-Tech Engineers), and FPI flows amid monsoon data and US policy shifts.

us.headline: US markets close higher as healthcare and financials lead; tech remains cautious amid Nvidia earnings test.
us.lead: US markets close higher as healthcare and financials lead; tech remains cautious amid Nvidia earnings test.
us.brief: S&P 500 and Nasdaq each gained 0.43% while the Dow jumped 0.98%, with Healthcare +1.3% and Financials +0.9% offsetting weak Tech (+0.1%) and Energy (-0.2%).
us.narrative:
US equities ended a positive day on August 24, 2026, with broad-based gains led by defensive and financial sectors. Healthcare stocks surged 1.3% while Financials climbed 0.9%, suggesting investor appetite for stability. Tech sector gained only 0.1% as markets brace for Nvidia's earnings report on Wednesday—a critical test of the global AI boom's health. The broader market strength was reflected in the S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) hitting $100 billion in assets, outperforming traditional market-weight indices by 3% year-to-date, signaling a shift toward smaller-cap strength.

Geopolitical and trade risks simmered beneath the surface. US-Canada trade negotiations collapsed, triggering 50% US tariffs on $20 billion in Canadian goods with retaliatory Canadian tariffs set for September 8. Meanwhile, the US Treasury announced fresh sanctions on Iran as gold climbed to a 3-month high of $4,627 per ounce, reflecting safe-haven demand. In Asia, Alibaba plunged after announcing a $10.2 billion share placement for AI infrastructure, while Shein lined up a $1.77 billion Hong Kong IPO at a $27 billion valuation—a sharp retreat from its $100 billion 2022 private valuation.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Defensive sector leads as financials also gain ground.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Results will signal health of global AI boom and tech sector.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Risk-on equity gains offset by trade tensions and geopolitical friction.

us.watch: Nvidia earnings Wednesday will determine if AI enthusiasm holds or if sector rotation away from tech accelerates further.
